summary: Iter145 — E2E verification of 4 new Cyber Crisis Commander features: (1) Connector Test Ping, (2) SITREP Preview/Note/Send-now, (3) Weekly Director Digest, (4) Connector-Quiet alert. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_iter145_crisis_ext.py — 12/12 PASS covering: POST /api/crisis/connectors/{crowdstrike,splunk,sentinel,servicenow,generic}/test returns {ok:true, vendor, mapped}, flips crisis_connector_health.last_received + increments count, and does NOT create a new crisis case; GET /api/crisis/cases/{ref}/sitrep/preview returns {title,text,note,cadence_hours}, PATCH sitrep_note persists and appears inside the composed preview text; POST /api/crisis/cases/{ref}/sitrep/send-now returns {posted,teams,slack} and writes a 'Manual SITREP sent to leadership chat' Communication timeline event (executed with self_scan._post_chat_alert monkey-patched to no-op so no live Teams/Slack post fired); GET & POST /api/crisis/settings persist director_digest, connector_quiet, connector_quiet_hours; run_weekly_director_digest returns 0 with toggle OFF and _build_director_digest returns (html,n) with a well-formed 'OBSERRA · CYBER CRISIS COMMANDER / Weekly Crisis Digest' template when n>=1; GET /api/crisis/connectors/quiet-check returns {threshold_hours, business_hours, enabled, quiet[]}; backdating a connector's last_received to -48h correctly flags it as quiet, a fresh test-ping resets quiet_alerted_at to null; run_connector_quiet_alerts returns 0 with toggle OFF (opt-in gate honoured); unauthenticated calls to /settings and /connectors/{vendor}/test return 401/403. Frontend: logged in as jblan2026@gmail.com, dismissed onboarding, /app/cyber-crisis-commander loaded cleanly (cyber-crisis-commander-page present). Incident Command tab: all 5 crisis-native-test-<vendor> buttons rendered; clicking crisis-native-test-crowdstrike flipped crisis-native-health-crowdstrike from '9 event(s)' -> 'Live · last received 8/12/2026, 8:50:50 PM · 10 event(s)'; crisis-connector-quiet strip + crisis-quiet-toggle render, toggle flipped 'Off'->'On' and back for cleanup. War Room tab: crisis-sitrep-console + crisis-sitrep-preview + crisis-sitrep-note + crisis-sitrep-save + crisis-sitrep-send-now all present; typing 'TEST_ITER145 UI note' + Save reflected the note inside the preview text; cleared afterwards. Board View tab: crisis-director-digest panel + crisis-digest-toggle + crisis-digest-send-now all present; toggle flipped 'Weekly digest: Off'->'Weekly digest: On' and back off (toast 'Weekly director digest disabled.' confirmed). Header crisis-more-btn opens crisis-more-menu with crisis-brief-cadence + crisis-sitrep-cadence. Cleanup: crisis_settings.director_digest=false, crisis_settings.connector_quiet=false; all TEST_ITER145 throwaway cases + events/snapshots/actions deleted; quiet_alerted_at reset via fresh ingest; sitrep_note reset to empty; CRISIS-0002 sitrep_schedule_hours preserved at 0. SITREP send-now was executed in-process against a throwaway case with _post_chat_alert monkey-patched (no live Teams/Slack). Director digest send-now endpoint was NOT invoked — verified via _build_director_digest + run_weekly_director_digest (opt-in off) instead, per test-request caution.
critical_code_review_comments: crisis_commander._send_director_digest (L2896-2903): the per-recipient try/except silently swallows every SMTP failure and still counts sent=0 without any audit trail. Consider logger.exception per failed recipient so operators can debug delivery issues (this is currently invisible in prod).

crisis_commander.director_digest_send_now (L2907-2915): when the org has 0 open crises we return {sent:0,crises:0,message:...} which is fine, but there is NO opt-in check on the send-now endpoint itself — an operator can force-send a digest regardless of the org's crisis_settings.director_digest toggle. If the toggle is intended as an org policy gate (not just a scheduler filter), send-now should also respect it (or explicitly bypass with an audit note).

crisis_commander._connector_quiet_scan (L2940-2965): uses raw datetime.now(timezone.utc) but _record_connector_health resets quiet_alerted_at only in the ingest path. If an operator runs the connector Test Ping to 'confirm wiring' after a real outage, quiet_alerted_at is silently cleared — a subsequent real quiet event will re-alert immediately. Acceptable, but worth documenting.

crisis_commander.sitrep_send_now (L2817-2844): the endpoint composes with _compose_sitrep BEFORE checking whether any channel is wired. If both teams/slack channels are absent, posted=False but a 'Manual SITREP sent to leadership chat' timeline event is still written. Consider distinguishing 'attempted' vs 'posted' in the audit title (e.g., 'Manual SITREP attempted (no chat wired)' when posted=False) to avoid misleading the timeline.

crisis_commander.CrisisSettingsBody.connector_quiet_hours (L2728): Field ge=1, le=72 — but the default returned by _crisis_settings is 6 when unset. If an admin explicitly wants 0 (disabled), they must instead flip the connector_quiet toggle; consider allowing 0 or documenting that only the toggle controls enablement.

crisis_commander._connector_quiet_scan does not filter out connectors that were never wired (last_received is truthy but count could be 1 from a Test Ping only). The scan will alert on a connector that ONLY ever received the synthetic test payload — arguably a false positive. Consider requiring count>=N or last_title != 'Connection test' before flagging.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All 4 iter145 features are green end-to-end. Backend endpoints: GET/POST /api/crisis/settings (director_digest, connector_quiet, connector_quiet_hours 1..72), POST /api/crisis/connectors/{vendor}/test (returns {ok,vendor,mapped,tested_at}), GET /api/crisis/cases/{ref}/sitrep/preview, POST /api/crisis/cases/{ref}/sitrep/send-now, POST /api/crisis/director-digest/send-now, GET /api/crisis/connectors/quiet-check. CrisisCaseUpdate now accepts sitrep_note (<=500 chars). Business-hours gate for connector-quiet is weekday 08:00-18:00 UTC. To test safely in-process: 'import self_scan; self_scan._post_chat_alert = <no-op>' and 'from kernel import notifications; notifications.send_email = <no-op>' BEFORE calling crisis_commander.run_weekly_director_digest / run_connector_quiet_alerts / any send-now endpoint. IMPORTANT: reuse a single asyncio loop across multiple in-process cc.* invocations — Motor's global executor is bound to the first loop it sees; two consecutive asyncio.run() calls will raise 'Event loop is closed'. See _shared_loop() helper in test_iter145_crisis_ext.py. Note on UI regression: this iteration's tab list correction — real tab data-testids are: crisis-tab-{mission,command,decisions,impact,response,warroom,recovery,regulatory,controls,timeline,briefing,board,defensibility}. The list in the review request (comms, actions, legal, postmortem, threat, exposure, reports) was wrong — command/warroom/board were exercised directly and the crisis page rendered cleanly with no white screen or hydration crashes.
rca of the issue: N/A — all features green. Two initial pytest failures were self-inflicted test bugs (parallel-xdist case-count race + Motor event-loop closed on second asyncio.run); fixed by (a) filtering new refs by title instead of counting rows, and (b) introducing a module-level _shared_loop() reused across in-process cc.* calls.
